exposure: Women with HSV-2/GH using suppressive antiviral therapy
Women with HSV-2/GH not using suppressive antiviral therapy
outcome: Intrapartum procedures (fetal scalp electrode, artificial rupture of membranes, intrauterine pressure catheter, operative vaginal delivery)
cohort: 449 pregnant women delivering at the University of Washington Medical center
finding: Provider awareness of genital herpes infection, through HSV serotesting or history, was associated with fewer invasive obstetric procedures but not with an increased rate of cesarean birth.
mod_finding: Provider awareness of genital herpes infection, whether through HSV serotesting or history, was linked to a decrease in invasive obstetric procedures known to be associated with neonatal herpes, but it did not lead to an increase in cesarean birth rates.
